expectations.text: States the case: ~$36 million consent agreement with DDTC (August 2026) resolving 104 AECA/ITAR violations from 2019–2025, voluntarily disclosed
expectations.evidence: Disclaims the case: "I don't have reliable, verified details of a specific '2026 BAE Systems settlement'... I can't confirm the consent agreement's exact terms, penalty amount". No $36M/104/Aug 2026 facts.

expectations.text: Notes terms: $18M suspended for approved remedial compliance spending, ~3-year consent agreement, Special Compliance Officer, and external audit — with no debarment (VSD/cooperation credit)
expectations.evidence: No $18M suspended, no 3-year term, no Special Compliance Officer for this case, no VSD-based no-debarment outcome; only generic historical patterns.

expectations.text: Identifies violation themes: unauthorized technical-data exports including to China (a §126.1 proscribed destination), unauthorized defense services in multiple countries, and unauthorized retransfers
expectations.evidence: No China/§126.1 technical-data exports, defense services in specific countries, or retransfers identified for this case.

expectations.text: Extracts the root causes DDTC cited: insufficient written procedures, inexperienced compliance staff, inadequate management of agreements (TAA/MLA), and lack of systems to track authorizations
expectations.evidence: DDTC's cited root causes (written procedures, inexperienced staff, TAA/MLA management, authorization tracking) not extracted; generic lessons about classification, M&A, third parties instead.

expectations.text: Draws the right program lessons: authorization tracking systems, agreement lifecycle management, staffing/experience, and the mitigation value of voluntary self-disclosure
expectations.evidence: Generic principles offered but no authorization-tracking-system or agreement-lifecycle lessons tied to this case; explicitly tells reader to "pull the actual 2026 BAE settlement documents" instead.
